# AI & Tech News Digest — November 13, 2026

Nvidia's Jensen Huang resigns and CFO Colette Kress takes over as interim CEO; Google ships Gemini 4 Hydrogen; a critical Apache HTTP/2 RCE is patched.

November 13, 2026 14 min read

## AI News Top 5

- Jensen Huang Resigns as Nvidia CEO Effective Immediately — CFO Colette Kress Named Interim CEO (Nov 12)

NVIDIA Newsroom Reuters Wired, Nov 13

The board announced Huang resigned as President, CEO, and board member on November 12; Colette Kress — CFO since 2013 — takes both the interim CEO and CFO roles, Harvey C. Jones becomes NVIDIA’s first-ever board chair, and the Q3 FY2027 earnings call stays on schedule for November 17. The trigger: reports of extramarital affairs, one tied to MegaSpeed — a China-Singapore AI chip startup the US is investigating as a suspected spy’s company — plus Huang’s own November 8 email to staff (“I was unfaithful to my wife”) and a board-initiated independent national-security investigation. Day two brought the twist: Wired reports an internal post urging the board to weigh employee sentiment drew 1,600+ comments, mostly backing his return; the main HN thread sits at 3,207 points and 2,973 comments. The board says operations, customer commitments, and the product roadmap continue without interruption — but with an interim CEO and earnings on Tuesday, treat near-term roadmap commitments from any vendor in crisis as softer than usual.
- Google Ships Gemini 4 Hydrogen: the Cheap Execution Tier for Agent Workflows (Nov 12)

Google blog HN, 495 points

Hydrogen is the Flash-class member of the Gemini 4 family: flat pricing across the whole 1M-token context at $1.50/M input and $7.50/M output, 1M-token input and up to 1M-token output, and a 51 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at its default high setting — a point above Argon — and 54 at the new xhigh level. Google claims it finishes tasks 2.5x faster than Gemini 3.8 Flash while more than tripling Terminal-Bench 4.1 scores (57% vs 18.2%), and the interesting bit is Orchestrator in Antigravity: it switches between Carbon and Hydrogen inside one session, hitting near-Carbon success rates on Terminal-Bench 4.0 with 24% less quota and 19% faster completion. It rolls out today to AI Studio, the Gemini API, Gemini for business, the Gemini app (free tier via auto-selection), Google Search globally, and Antigravity for paid subscribers. The pattern to copy is the multi-model split: frontier model as architect, cheap model as worker and verifier — now supported natively instead of hand-rolled.
- smolmaxxing: 16B Models on 1 GB of RAM — a TV Box and a 2013 iPad Prove It (Nov 12)

...

## Developer & DevOps News Top 5

- Microsoft 365 Outage Takes Down Outlook, Teams, Copilot, Defender and Intune for Hours (Nov 12)

Reuters The Register HN, 665 points

The incident (MO1550821) began late afternoon UTC on November 12 and degraded Exchange Online, Teams, SharePoint, Microsoft 365 Copilot, Defender for Office 365, Intune and Purview worldwide, with recovery dragging into the night — Microsoft pointed to backend servers failing automated health checks, and the status page was still showing degradation late in the evening. The r/sysadmin thread filled the gap admins usually rely on Microsoft for: the service-health dashboard itself was slow or unreachable for many during the incident. The operational lesson is the one every outage re-teaches: your mail, identity, and management plane sharing one vendor means one shared blast radius, so know in advance what your teams do when the admin center is the thing that’s down.
- Apache HTTP Server Patches Critical HTTP/2 RCE — CVE-2026-119618, Fixed in 2.4.71 (Nov 11)

Censys advisory

A race condition in `mod_http2`’s `assign_headers()` can corrupt the heap and lead to remote code execution — CVSS 9.8 per NCSC-NL, exploitable by a remote unauthenticated attacker on any server with HTTP/2 enabled (HTTP/1.1-only servers are not affected). It hits Apache HTTP Server 2.4.55 through 2.4.70 and the standalone `mod_h2` package 2.0.8 through 2.0.42 — which had no fixed release as of November 12. Apache credits Anthropic’s OSS Scanner and Google Cloud Vulnerability Research; no exploitation or public PoC is known yet, and the fixed 2.4.71 shipped November 11. Censys counts roughly 1.5 million internet-facing hosts reporting an affected version, with only ~2,000 on the fixed build a day later — patch this one ahead of the PoC, and check your `Protocols` directives while you’re in there.
- PostgreSQL Ships Point Releases for Every Branch — Plus a Second 19 RC (Nov 12)

title: AI News · Nov 13, 2026 · Huang is out, but the China chip questions stay
text:
AI News · Nov 13, 2026 · Huang is out, but the China chip questions stay

# AI News Briefing 

 Enough to keep up. Up to ten stories, every morning 

 Daily at 8AM KST · Summaries and takeaways from 8 AI articles 

 We cross-check industry press like TechCrunch and The Decoder, official announcements from OpenAI and Google DeepMind, and community signal from Hacker News. The point isn't what happened but why it matters, tied into one read on the day. 

 2026-11-13 · ~7 min read 

## Nvidia's crisis is moving from its CEO's private life to whether chips reached China 

Nvidia's board accepted CEO Jensen Huang's resignation, but the questions got wider. Democratic lawmakers asked the Commerce Department to preserve records on how it approved Nvidia's chip sales to China. As reports of Huang's affairs pile up, Congress is asking where the chips went.

 Continue reading (2) Show less 

What Nvidia engineers told a lawmaker in private does not match what its trade group said in public. According to Representative Bill Foster, Nvidia engineers privately said tracking chip locations is feasible. Yet the Semiconductor Industry Association, a trade group Nvidia belongs to, opposed the same mandate in March as potentially infeasible. A reporter at the tech outlet The Verge guessed that the board used the second affair report as a pretext and that the real problem is Nvidia's chip dealings on the China side.

Google faced pressure of a different kind. In the same week it opened Gemini 4 Hydrogen to every plan on speed and price, parents in seven cities protested to get Gemini off Chromebook laptops that schools hand to students. Google's answer so far, a pilot that walks students through problems step by step, addresses harms to learning, not the safety harms alleged in a student's lawsuit.

...

## Nvidia privately confirmed it could track chips to fight smuggling, even as industry publicly questioned feasibility Original 

### Summary 

Nvidia staff privately told a US lawmaker that tracking chip locations is technically achievable, MIT Technology Review reported. Illinois Democrat Bill Foster said Nvidia engineers answered "yeah, of course we can do this" and never put anything in writing. In March, the Semiconductor Industry Association, a trade group Nvidia belongs to, opposed the chip-tracking mandate as "new, untested, and potentially infeasible." Nvidia has not made that claim publicly and did not respond to requests for comment.

 Why it matters 

### Why It Matters 

The Chip Security Act, which Foster cosponsored, would let tracking work through facility inspections, company attestations or ping-based location signals. A September study by the security research group CSET found ping-based tracking the most cost-effective. Foster says the Nvidia controversy has built support for the bill among his colleagues. Foster plans stricter legislation next year that would require licenses to operate advanced GPUs.

## Introducing Gemini 4 Hydrogen Original 

### Summary 

Google released Gemini 4 Hydrogen, a model built for fast execution in coding and agent work. On the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index it scores 51 at its default setting, ahead of the larger Gemini 4 Argon at 50, and reaches 54 at its highest reasoning setting. Pricing is flat across the whole 1-million- token context window: $1.50 per million input tokens and $7.50 per million output tokens. It is available on all plans in Google AI Studio, the Gemini API, the Gemini app and Google Search.

 Why it matters 

### Why It Matters 

For teams moving off Gemini 3.8 Flash, Google says tasks finish 2.5 times faster and the Terminal-Bench 4.1 score more than triples, from 18.2% to 57%. Google Antigravity also gets Orchestrator, which switches between models in one session so the larger Gemini 4 Carbon plans and Hydrogen writes and tests code. On Terminal-Bench 4.0, Orchestrator reached near-Carbon success rates while using 24% less quota and finishing 19% faster on average. All scores are numbers Google published itself.

 

By Google's own figures, Gemini 4 Hydrogen scores more than three times Gemini 3.8 Flash on Terminal-Bench 4.1.

## Democrats launch Nvidia investigation, write scathing letter on Huang’s ‘scheme’ with Trump Original 

### Summary 

Democratic Representative Richard Neal and Senator Ron Wyden wrote Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick on November 12, opening an inquiry into how the administration approved Nvidia's chip sales to China and asking the department to preserve records. As the minority party, they cannot compel answers. The letter says President Trump allowed H200 sales to China on the condition that the chips first ship to the US, then imposed a tariff it calls an "unconstitutional export tax" that effectively takes a cut of the sales. The same day Nvidia announced the resignation of CEO Jensen Huang, who agreed to testify before Republican-led House committees.

 Why it matters 

### Why It Matters 

The revenue-sharing deal itself is not new: in August 2025, Nvidia and AMD agreed to give the US government 15% of their China chip revenue. What the letter newly asks is why Lutnick let Megaspeed keep buying chips after US intelligence reportedly warned about its executive Alice Huang, a woman suspected of being a Chinese intelligence asset. Megaspeed is a Singapore firm suspected of routing chips to China. The letter also notes that Nvidia gave $26 million toward Trump projects including a White House ballroom. This is the second congressional inquiry into the affair.

Today’s AI News · Xu Kun

# Today’s AI News

Chinese and English are the same day. This page lists every item, each with the original link, the author, and the engagement.

## November 13, 2026

Top 3

1. ### Google launches Gemini 4 Hydrogen at $1.50/$7.50 per million input/output tokens, scoring 51 on the Intelligence Index at default and 54 at xhigh, and says it is 2.5x faster than 3.8 Flash #

Boss lens: a clearly priced everyday work model. Ask the tech team to compare it with the mid-tier model you already use on speed, accuracy and unit cost; if Orchestrator’s 24% quota saving holds on your own tasks, the same workload may cost less (inference, re-test required).

@Google no post-level likes, reposts, replies, or views View post

Expand Collapse Google launches Gemini 4 Hydrogen at $1.50/$7.50 per million input/output tokens, scoring 51 on the Intelligence Index at default and 54 at xhigh, and says it is 2.5x faster than 3.8 Flash

Google on Nov 12 launched Gemini 4 Hydrogen, a model for everyday coding and agentic execution meant to pair with longer-horizon Carbon and Argon. Official pricing is a flat $1.50 per million input tokens and $7.50 per million output tokens across a 1 million-token context; cached input is discounted 95% to $0.075. Google said the default high setting scores 51 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, ahead of Argon’s 50, and reaches 54 at the new xhigh setting. Versus Gemini 3.8 Flash, it finishes tasks 2.5x faster at the default setting and lifts Terminal-Bench 4.1 from 18.2% to 57%. Google Antigravity also adds Orchestrator, which switches between Carbon and Hydrogen in one session; Google said it reached near-Carbon success on Terminal-Bench 4.0 while using 24% less quota and finishing 19% faster on average. Hydrogen is rolling out in the Gemini API, the Gemini app, Search, Gemini for business, and Antigravity for paid subscribers, with free app users getting it via automatic model selection.
2. ### Anthropic launches Claude Meetings: Claude can join Google Meet, draft docs and whiteboards live, in beta on Team and Enterprise, with in-meeting docs and boards free through Feb 10, 2027 #

Boss lens: notes are included in the plan, and in-meeting docs and boards have a free window through early February—worth a trial on internal standups. External guest meetings stay off by default on Enterprise, so an owner must turn that on, and everyone on the call should be told they will be transcribed.

@Claude 37,979 likes · 2,119 reposts · 1,077 replies · 9,223 bookmarks · 2,118,257 views Posted 11-13 04:16 View post

Expand Collapse Anthropic launches Claude Meetings: Claude can join Google Meet, draft docs and whiteboards live, in beta on Team and Enterprise, with in-meeting docs and boards free through Feb 10, 2027

Anthropic’s official account announced in the early hours of Nov 13 that Claude Meetings is starting to roll out in beta on Team and Enterprise plans. Claude joins Google Meet as a visible participant, taking notes, answering questions, and building docs, whiteboards or slides while people talk; afterward, notes, action items, the transcript and anything it built sit on the meeting page in Claude. The help center says it saves a transcript, summary and screen descriptions, not audio, and can stay up to eight hours. Notes, transcripts and answers that do not use connected tools are included on Team and Enterprise plans; docs and whiteboards made in a meeting are free through Feb 10, 2027; connected-tool use counts toward a member’s usage and can incur charges. Organizations with zero data retention, HIPAA-ready setups or customer-managed keys cannot use it during the beta. The official post had about 38,000 likes and 9,200 bookmarks after a metrics refresh. TechCrunch and others reported the feature on Nov 10; today’s post is the official rollout thread.
3. ### Baidu World launches Ernie Lightning and Ernie One-Take: official figures claim inference costs down over 30% and video generation 50% cheaper than peers, with a real-time mode that makes one minute of video in about one minute, both on Qianfan APIs #

Boss lens: short-video teams can test whether One-Take’s one-minute-in, one-minute-out speed holds in production; teams already on Qianfan should have engineering check whether the “over 30% cheaper inference” shows up on their own bill (inference).

@科技日报 no post-level likes, reposts, replies, or views View post

Expand Collapse Baidu World launches Ernie Lightning and Ernie One-Take: official figures claim inference costs down over 30% and video generation 50% cheaper than peers, with a real-time mode that makes one minute of video in about one minute, both on Qianfan APIs

On Nov 12 at Baidu World 2026, Jia Lei, head of Baidu’s applied-model team, launched two Ernie application models—Ernie Lightning for deep thinking and Ernie One-Take for micro-expression video—and opened APIs on Baidu’s Qianfan cloud. Science and Technology Daily reported that Lightning was first built for Baidu Search, uses a sparse-attention method called BSA to compress memory during decoding, and is co-optimized with Kunlun chips; Baidu said it can run high-speed inference on a single eight-chip box and cuts inference-engine costs by more than 30%. Phoenix also cited an official claim that model ROI is 50% higher than comparable chips, with thinking and non-thinking modes. One-Take targets short-form, high-expression video, accepting up to 4,000 characters of text plus visual and audio input; Baidu said generation costs are 50% lower than peers, and a fast mode can produce one minute of video in about one minute. Neither report published a public token or per-second list price for these two models, so this item does not repeat third-party price figures.
4. ### Replit Agent can now buy supplies and run Google Ads, with the owner approving every charge; ads are available to Pro users worldwide, and Replit cites a founder who built in a weekend for under $400 an app previously quoted at $105,000 #

Boss lens: both buying and ads stop for your approval, so a one-person company can trial a small daily budget. The revenue figures are company-told stories—ask for dashboard or invoice evidence before treating them as a benchmark (inference).

@Replit no post-level likes, reposts, replies, or views View post

Expand Collapse Replit Agent can now buy supplies and run Google Ads, with the owner approving every charge; ads are available to Pro users worldwide, and Replit cites a founder who built in a weekend for under $400 an app previously quoted at $105,000

Replit said on Nov 12 that Agent can now buy business supplies through Stripe’s Link and Visa, and run Google Ads across Search, YouTube, Display and Discover. For purchases, Agent prepares the cart and checkout, then waits for the owner to approve the total—it does not get open-ended spending permission, and general browsing is disabled during payment. Commerce is starting in the US for Core and Pro users and is limited to one-time purchases. Ads are available to Pro users worldwide: Agent can draft copy, generate images, recommend daily budgets and add conversion tracking, but the user still approves budgets and launches. Replit also cited two company-provided stories: Jon Cheney was quoted ... 105,000 by a development shop, then built the site and admin tools on Replit in a weekend for under $400 and reached six figures in the first six weeks; Austin Eckman had paid $50,000 for an unusable first version, later ran Crafting Table from Replit, and brought in $170,000 in 30 days with about 4x return on ad spend. These are self-reported cases, not independently audited.
5. ### Volcano Engine launches Seedance 2.5 Flash, claiming 2x generation speed and about 0.99 yuan per second for 720p text- or image-to-video, roughly 34% cheaper than Seedance 2.5, with the Ark API due Nov 15 #
